prompt: A single detailed cutaway illustration, drawn like a cross between a technical diagram and an editorial drawing. At the top, a sleek grey stealth cruise missile in flight, its body sliced open to reveal a tiny green circuit-board computer sitting inside — clearly a mass-market hobbyist module, still bearing a retail-style label. A dotted line runs from that module to a rounded inset panel showing what the missile's camera sees: a grey landscape from above with one vehicle outlined by a recognition box, illustrating machine-vision guidance in the final seconds of flight. At the bottom, a documentary workbench scene: gloved hands with tweezers lifting the same small module out of an opened missile casing, beside a grid of 35 tiny chips and parts laid out on a mat like evidence, each tagged with a small country label (USA, Switzerland, Japan, China, Belarus). The overall mood is quiet and anatomical rather than dramatic — a forensic drawing of how ordinary consumer technology ends up inside a weapon.
